sections.title: Multiple Representations of Relationships
sections.learning_target: Students will connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
i_can_statements: I can construct a table, graph, equation, or context from another representation of the same relationship.
I can use features in one representation to work with a related table, graph, equation, or context.
I can determine whether two representations belong to the same relationship using evidence from values, rates, or patterns.
misconceptions_failure_points: Matching representations by visual appearance while ignoring scale or values.
Changing a table or graph without preserving the same ordered pairs or relationship.
modeling_application_practice: Build a graph from a context about distance, cost, or time.
Formulate an equation from a table of values.
Use a graph to predict a missing table value.
Check whether a context and equation communicate the same relationship.

spiral.current_learning: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
spiral.retrieval: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.
spiral.mastery: Solve inequalities, represent solution sets graphically, and interpret solutions in context.

sections.title: Inputs, Outputs, and Functions
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
i_can_statements: I can formulate a rule that connects inputs to outputs in a table, graph, equation, or context.
I can apply an input-output rule to generate missing values and ordered pairs.
I can assess whether a rule gives one output for each input in a situation.
misconceptions_failure_points: Reversing inputs and outputs when applying a rule.
Treating a repeated input with two different outputs as a function.
modeling_application_practice: Build a function rule from repeated input-output calculations.
Use a context to assign inputs and outputs meaning.
Predict outputs for new inputs using a rule.
Check a mapping for repeated inputs with different outputs.

spiral.current_learning: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
spiral.retrieval: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.
spiral.mastery: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions correctly using substitution and order of operations.

sections.title: Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
i_can_statements: I can design examples of linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value relationships using more than one representation.
I can extend patterns in tables, graphs, equations, and contexts to work with common function families.
I can critique a proposed function family choice using evidence from rate of change, shape, or equation structure.
misconceptions_failure_points: Classifying a family from graph appearance alone without checking differences, ratios, or equation structure.
Confusing quadratic growth with exponential growth.
modeling_application_practice: Create a context that fits a given family feature.
Use table patterns to choose a likely family.
Predict how a graph changes when a family pattern changes.
Critique family choices that rely only on appearance.

spiral.current_learning: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
spiral.retrieval: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Accurately perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals while interpreting results in mathematical and contextual situations.

sections.title: Expressions and Structure
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
i_can_statements: I can build equivalent expressions by using structure, grouping, and properties of operations.
I can apply rewriting strategies to make the meaning of an expression easier to work with.
I can determine whether two expressions are equivalent by using structure, substitution, or properties.
misconceptions_failure_points: Combining unlike terms as though they were like terms.
Distributing a factor to only one term or changing the value while rewriting.
modeling_application_practice: Build an expression for a cost, perimeter, or repeated quantity.
Rewrite an expression to reveal a useful structure.
Use substitution to test equivalence.
Connect terms and coefficients to a context.

spiral.current_learning: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
spiral.retrieval: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.
spiral.mastery: Analyze and rewrite algebraic expressions using properties of operations and algebraic structure.

sections.title: Rate of Change and Slope

Use table patterns to model constant change
Represent increasing and decreasing rates with graph features

Section Outline: Section 2.1: Rate of Change and Slope Learning Target: Students will interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change. I Can Statements I can construct rate-of-change statements from tables, graphs, and situations. I can apply slope calculations to interpret constant change between quantities. I can determine whether a slope value is reasonable for a given context. Key Vocabulary / Notation slope rate of change rise/run positive/negative/zero/undefined slope Key Representations Slope triangles on coordinate graphs Tables showing equal input intervals Contextual rate statements Ratio notation for vertical change over horizontal change Positive, negative, zero, and undefined slope examples Common Misconceptions / Failure Points Reversing vertical and horizontal change or using inconsistent point order. Interpreting slope as a starting value rather than a rate. Modeling / Application / Practice Opportunities Connect speed, cost per item, and growth rates to slope Build verbal interpretations for slopes in real situations Use table patterns to model constant change Represent increasing and decreasing rates with graph features Spiral Planning Intro: Interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change. Review: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language. Mastery: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.

Section 2.2: Graphing Linear Functions Learning Target: Students will graph linear functions and interpret key features. I Can Statements I can build graphs of linear functions using slope and intercept information. I can use key features of a line to interpret a relationship. I can extend a graph to predict outputs within a meaningful range. Key Vocabulary / Notation slope intercept $y=mx+b$ linear graph scale Key Representations Coordinate plane graphs Slope-intercept form Intercepts and starting values Tables generated from linear rules Contextual graphs with labeled axes Common Misconceptions / Failure Points Plotting the intercept on the wrong axis. Using slope steps without respecting graph scale or sign. Modeling / Application / Practice Opportunities Graph savings, distance, or subscription situations Use intercepts to represent initial values Connect slope direction to increasing or decreasing behavior Create graphs from equations and contextual descriptions Spiral Planning Intro: Graph linear functions and interpret key features. Review: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship. Mastery: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.

Section 2.3: Writing Linear Equations Learning Target: Students will write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations. I Can Statements I can formulate linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations. I can apply slope-intercept structure to connect rate and starting value. I can design equivalent equations that represent the same linear relationship. Key Vocabulary / Notation slope-intercept form slope initial value $m$ $b$ Key Representations Slope-intercept equations Tables of input-output values Graphs with marked intercepts Verbal descriptions of rates and starting values Equivalent equation forms Common Misconceptions / Failure Points Using an arbitrary table value as the intercept. Confusing the roles of $m$ and $b$ in $y=mx+b$. Modeling / Application / Practice Opportunities Write rules for cell phone plans, savings, or distance Translate graphs into equations Use tables to calculate slope and initial value Revise equations to make context features visible Spiral Planning Intro: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations. Review: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms. Mastery: Represent linear relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and contextual descriptions.

Section 2.4: Comparing Linear Representations Learning Target: Students will analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations. I Can Statements I can construct comparison models for linear relationships shown in different forms. I can use slope and intercept information to interpret similarities and differences. I can critique conclusions about linear relationships using evidence from representations. Key Vocabulary / Notation slope intercept rate starting value equivalent relationship Key Representations Pairs of graphs Tables with different scales Equations in slope-intercept form Contextual descriptions Feature comparison organizers Common Misconceptions / Failure Points Comparing lines only by current output values instead of rate and starting value. Assuming the steeper-looking graph has greater slope without checking axis scales. Modeling / Application / Practice Opportunities Compare competing plans or rates Use representations to support choices Translate unlike representations into common features Check claims about which relationship grows faster Spiral Planning Intro: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations. Review: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts. Mastery: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.

Section 2.5: Linear Modeling with Data Learning Target: Students will use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data. I Can Statements I can design linear models that represent patterns in real-world data. I can predict values using a linear model and interpret the result. I can assess whether a linear model fits a data situation well enough for the question being asked. Key Vocabulary / Notation linear model data trend prediction model fit Key Representations Scatter plots Lines of fit Tables of real-world data Linear model equations Residual-style reasonableness observations Common Misconceptions / Failure Points Treating every data set as perfectly linear. Using a prediction far outside the meaningful data range without considering model limits. Modeling / Application / Practice Opportunities Model trends in measurement, cost, or time data Use lines of fit to make predictions Interpret slope and intercept in data contexts Discuss when linear models are useful or limited Spiral Planning Intro: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data. Review: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations. Mastery: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.
